messages:
alex_g: heads up — I opened a tiny terraform + k8s change to switch the inference svc to NLB for TLS passthrough. can someone sanity-check the annotations?

alex_g: current plan (in the PR) is:
```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: "tcp"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-cert: "arn:aws:acm:..."  # temporary for test
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-type: "ip"
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local
  ports:
    - port: 443
      targetPort: 8080
```

alex_g: main question: is the cert annotation ignored when using NLB passthrough? I think we should use Gateway API with secretRef instead but wanted to confirm operational gotchas.

maria_dev: quick answers — for TLS passthrough you generally don't terminate on the NLB, so aws-load-balancer-ssl-cert won't be used. that annotation is only for TLS termination at the LB (ALB or NLB TLS mode). if you need end-to-end TLS you want the Gateway API or a node/sidecar cert.

maria_dev: if you stick with the Service LB approach and want NLB passthrough, you need target-type=ip and to make sure backend pod is speaking TLS on 8080. also confirm externalTrafficPolicy: Local to preserve client source IP if you rely on it.

kevin_ops: fwiw we ran into a quirk: when externalTrafficPolicy is Local + targetType ip + rollout across AZs, you can get uneven distribution if some nodes have no endpoints. add a readiness-check during rollout canary or use internal gate to avoid blackholes.

kevin_ops: also if you plan to use PROXY protocol (for passing client src ip) the annotation is `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-proxy-protocol: '*''` but that requires your pod to accept PROXY v1/v2. not all ingress controllers do.

alex_g: good point, we don't want proxy-protocol parsing in the app. assume no PROXY protocol. we do rely on client ip for some rate limiting, might rely on X-Forwarded-For from a sidecar.

maria_dev: if you want Gateway API route TLS with secretRef, config looks like: 
```yaml
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: TLSSecret
metadata:
  name: inference-cert
spec:
  secretName: inference-tls
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Gateway
# ... listeners.tls.certificateRefs -> secretRef { name: inference-cert }
```
This keeps certs in k8s secrets and works with our private deployment KMS-backed secrets.

alex_g: terraform side: I added a variable `nlb_enable_tls_passthrough` and wired it to annotation map. any naming nitpicks?

kevin_ops: looks fine. suggest default false and enable only for the inference namespace via terragrunt varsets or a per-cluster flag. and include a sentinel check in the module: if tls_passthrough == true && target_type != "ip" -> error.

maria_dev: also add an explanatory comment in the module README — folks keep trying to set ssl-cert on NLB and get confused. small doc saves time.

deploy-bot: CI: terraform fmt passed, tfplan produced changes: + aws_lb (nlb) expected. kubernetes: manifest lint found 1 warning: "externalTrafficPolicy: Local may cause imbalance if endpoints are not spread across nodes".

alex_g: thanks bot. i'll add a note in the PR about rollout strategy (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%).

maria_dev: ping me when ready and i'll review the Gateway API secret wiring. i want to confirm KMS key ARN used for the secret encryption is the same as private cluster standard.

kevin_ops: small test suggestion — deploy a test svc with nginx that speaks TLS on 8443, point NLB to it, and curl through in each AZ to verify passthrough works before flipping the real service. saved us before.

alex_g: will do the test, update PR with docs + terraform sentinel check + rollout steps. pinging reviewers: @maria_dev @kevin_ops please review when you have a minute. :pray: 

maria_dev: ack, will take a look later today. :thumbsup:

kevin_ops: on it, should be quick.

alex_g: thanks — closing loop after tests. :)
